svg.title: The types a forecast passes through, and what each rules out
svg.desc: Six steps from top to bottom. The row reader produces ObservedRow values with what each row measures. The fit builds a TrainingPartition from them, a row count and a digest per stream, and records it in fit.meta.json. A later command reads the partition back, checked against the data. ForecastPlan takes its origin from the partition and lists the targets. The forecast driver runs a particle filter per parameter draw over the training rows and the targets. camdl score scores each target against an outcome row. Beside each step is the invalid state it rules out.
svg.text: TYPE OR RECORD
WHAT IT RULES OUT
ObservedRow, Measures
one data row and the instant or period it measures
a training or scoring decision made from a row's label:
the reader computes Measures once, and later code reads only that
TrainingPartition::from_cutoff / whole
TrainingPartition
per stream, a RowPrefix: a row count and a digest
a row on both sides of the split, or a split with gaps:
a row trained exactly when its position is below the count
record()
fit.meta.json: training_partition
the partition as the fit recorded it
a later command deriving a different split: read() takes the
recorded counts and refuses rows that no longer match the digest
TrainingPartition::read
ForecastPlan, Target
the origin and every stream's targets
an origin other than the training extent (new() takes no origin);
a target, or its held-out row, ending at or before the origin
fixed_origin_forecast
forecast driver: StateConditioning
one particle filter per parameter draw
a row after the origin changing a weight: held-out values enter
as ObsCell::HeldOut, which the filter evaluates and never assimilates
held-out log-likelihoods, draws
camdl score
scores each target against its outcome row
outcomes from a different series: the outcome file must begin
with the rows the prediction conditioned on (checked by row digest)
